stem:
Kai, 20 months, has looked pale for some weeks. He drinks about 1.2 litres of cow's milk a day, much of it from a bottle overnight, and eats little meat. He is active and well, with no murmur, bruising or organomegaly.

| Result | Value | Reference range |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Haemoglobin | 86 g/L | 105-135 |
| MCV | 58 fL | 70-86 |
| Ferritin | 4 µg/L | 10-60 |

White cells and platelets are normal.

Which initial management is most appropriate?

options.label: A
options.text: Red cell transfusion, then an iron-rich diet
options.explanation: RCH notes that blood transfusion is rarely required in iron deficiency. He is active, with no signs of cardiac compromise, and oral iron will correct his anaemia.

options.label: B
options.text: Oral iron, with cow's milk under 500 mL a day
options.explanation: Correct. Excess cow's milk is a classic cause of iron deficiency in toddlers. RCH treats it with oral iron 3-6 mg/kg/day and limits cow's milk to under 500 mL a day, with more iron-rich foods.

options.label: C
options.text: Oral iron until his haemoglobin is normal
options.explanation: Stopping when the haemoglobin normalises leaves his stores empty. RCH continues iron for at least 3 months after the anaemia has been corrected, then checks ferritin.

options.label: D
options.text: IV iron infusion, then review in 3 months
options.explanation: RCH considers IV iron for poor adherence, malabsorption, ongoing blood loss or failure of an oral trial. None applies to a toddler who has not yet had oral iron.

options.label: E
options.text: Toddler formula in place of milk, and no iron
options.explanation: Changing his milk alone does not treat established iron deficiency anaemia; he needs iron supplements as well as a diet with less milk and more iron-rich food.

context: Iron deficiency from excess cow's milk: oral iron 3-6 mg/kg/day, cow's milk under 500 mL a day and more iron-rich foods; keep iron going 3 months after the Hb corrects. Transfusion is rarely needed.
